To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Dialogic inner speech is a distinct cognitive phenomenon from monologic inner speech; (2) Dialogic inner-speech generation is associated with activation of the default network; (3) Dialogic inner-speeche generation is associated with right temporal lobe activation that overlaps with activation associated with Theory-of-Mind reasoning.

dialogic inner speech (i.e. inner speech involving conversations) was associated with activation of a network including bilateral superior and middle temporal gyri, posterior cingulated and precuneus cortices, and left inferior and superior medial frontal gyri, and that this network was also activated by Theory of Mind (ToM) and perspective-taking tasks.
dialogic inner speech is associated with a widespread network involving temporal and frontal regions.
